# Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups (P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport) with low-level enemy threats

## Problem statement

Four power-up types in the GDD catalogue — **P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport** — cannot demonstrate their full behaviour without threats: Shield must absorb a hit, Bomb must clear on-screen enemy bullets, Phase Shift must pass through enemies and bullets, and Teleport must search for a safe spot free of threats. The operator split these "combat-coupled" types out of the threat-free power-up gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) into this dedicated **combat gym scene** that contains a **low-level enemy threat (E1 Scout with shooting)**. The scene shares the round-robin spawn lifecycle, grow-shrink animation, 3% collection threshold, player ship, and standalone HUD class with the non-combat gym, on which this item depends.

## Users

- **Player / developer testing the game** — wants to see each combat-coupled power-up's full effect against real (but low-level) threats: a shield bubble popping on a hit, a bomb wiping a bullet cloud, ghosting straight through a formation, and blinking away to a safe spot.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need the threat-coupled behaviour (hit absorption, bullet clearing, intangibility, safe-spot resolution) implemented and tested once, in a form the main game can reuse.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my shield bubble to absorb exactly one hit and pop, so I can verify the GDD's "absorbs one hit" rule.
- As a **player**, I want to collect a Bomb while scouts are firing and see every on-screen enemy bullet vanish, with enemies untouched (they are 1 HP, GDD §4.4).
- As a **player**, I want Phase Shift to let me fly straight through the scout formation and its bullets without being hit, for 3 seconds.
- As a **player**, I want to press Space with a collected Teleport to jump to the nearest safe spot (free of scouts and bullets) along my travel direction, gaining Phase Shift on arrival.
- As a **developer**, I want the ship's hit response (no shield/phase shift) to be a simple flash/reset with no lives counter, so the demo keeps a pure combat focus.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Combat scene with ship + low-level threats:** A new `GymPowerUpsCombat` scene (key `GymPowerUpsCombat`, label `PowerUps Combat`) is defined in `src/scenes/gym/`, auto-discovered and listed by the gym index, boots correctly, renders the player ship with standard thrust movement + screen-wrap, and contains a **formation of E1 Scout enemies** (reusing `src/entities/Scout.ts` + the formation utilities) with a **SHOOT toggle** that enables aimed enemy fire at the **ship's live position** (not the fixed demo target), so hits are demonstrable. Shared "← INDEX" back button present.
- [ ] **AC2 — Round-robin spawn/lifecycle:** The scene spawns exactly the combat-coupled power-ups **P3, P4, P6, P7 in ascending GDD order**, one every 5 s, each remaining stationary for a 5 s lifetime; spawn = **grow from scale 0 to full size**, despawn = **shrink to nothing**; growth/shrink delta-time driven with the same tunable constants as the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- [ ] **AC3 — Collection rule:** A drop is collectible only while its current scale is **> 3% of full size** (grow, hold, and shrink until below threshold); collection requires the ship to overlap the drop; an uncollected drop fades with no effect.
- [ ] **AC4 — P3 Shield full behaviour:** Collecting P3 arms a shield bubble rendered around the ship for **15 s**; the bubble **absorbs exactly one hit** (enemy body or enemy bullet) and then pops (effect ends, no ship flash/reset for that hit); if never hit, it expires after 15 s. Re-collection while active refreshes the timer to 15 s.
- [ ] **AC5 — P4 Bomb full behaviour:** Collecting P4 instantly removes **all on-screen enemy bullets** (aimed scout fire in-flight), does **not damage enemies** (GDD §4.4 note), is not a timed effect, and shows a brief HUD notice. Re-collection while enemies are not firing is a benign no-op (bullets cleared anyway).
- [ ] **AC6 — P6 Phase Shift full behaviour:** Collecting P6 renders a ghost-outline ship for **3 s** during which the ship **passes through enemy bodies and enemy bullets without being hit**; hit checks are disabled for the duration. Re-collection refreshes the timer to 3 s.
- [ ] **AC7 — P7 Teleport full behaviour:** P7 **stacks FIFO** (each pickup = one use); pressing **Space** consumes the earliest-collected use and teleports the ship **along the current travel direction to the nearest safe spot** — a position free of enemy bodies and enemy bullets in a safety radius, clamped to screen bounds; if no safe spot exists in the travel direction, the ship teleports to the nearest on-screen safe position anyway; on arrival the ship **gains P6 Phase Shift (3 s)** per GDD. HUD shows the teleport count.
- [ ] **AC8 — Hit response (no shield/phase shift):** Being hit by an enemy body or enemy bullet with no active P3/P6 triggers a **simple flash/reset with no lives counter** (e.g., brief invulnerability + reposition), per operator decision; this is the only consequence — no lives, no game over.
- [ ] **AC9 — HUD reuse:** The scene uses the **standalone HUD class from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) unchanged for active-effect icons, names, timers (P3/P6), and counts (P7); **no lives counter** in this scene; the HUD class itself is not modified with gym/combat-specific logic (any extension lives in the scene).
- [ ] **AC10 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover: P3 absorb-then-pop on a hit + 15 s expiry + refresh; P4 clearing all bullets without enemy damage; P6 pass-through (no hits during 3 s) + refresh; P7 FIFO stack/consume, safe-spot resolution (avoiding scouts/bullets, clamped), fallback when no safe spot, and P6-on-arrival; hit-response flash/reset (no lives); round-robin order. Scene-level tests (gameHarness) verify discovery, ship presence, scout formation + SHOOT toggle, collection against live bullets, and back button. Full suite green.
- [ ] **AC11 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (GDD §6.4 architecture gains `GymPowerUpsCombat`).
- [ ] **AC12 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). Neon-vector aesthetic; code-drawn graphics only — **no external art assets**; icons code-drawn per GDD §4.4 suggestions.
- **Threats:** **E1 Scout only** (operator decision) — reuse `src/entities/Scout.ts` as-is; formation via existing utilities; **shooting toggle** enabled for the demo (bullets aimed at the ship's live position). No E2/E3/E4/E5/Boss.
- **No lives model:** hit response is flash/reset only (operator decision); P8 lives is out of scope (it lives in the non-combat gym).
- **Weapon power-ups out of scope:** P1/P2/new weapon patterns belong to AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR; the ship's auto-fire is NOT part of this scene (Bomb does not damage enemies, so no fire needed).
- **Shared mechanics:** the spawn cadence (one per 5 s, 5 s lifetime, 0.5 s grow/shrink) and the 3% collection threshold match the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT); constants stay in `src/core/constants.ts`; the HUD class is reused unchanged (dependency on that item).
- **Hit model details:** overlap = ship hull radius + enemy/bullet radius, exactly as the GDD "enemies are the bullets" §2.4 model; shield/phase-shift suppress the hit response; teleport safe radius is a tunable constant (proposal: ~3× ship size).

## Existing state

- Non-combat power-up gym **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (intake_complete, open) delivers, first: `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` (base lifecycle), the type catalogue + icons, `src/ui/HUD.ts` (standalone), the spawn/lifecycle constants, and `GymPowerUps` — **this item depends on those reusable pieces**. This item adds the P3/P4/P6/P7 catalogue entries + threat-coupled effect hooks.
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` exists with `tryFireAimedBullet` (currently aimed at a fixed demo target), formation offsets, alive/destroy lifecycle; `GymScout` demonstrates a V-formation with EXPLODE/SHOOT buttons via the shared `GymFormationScene` core library (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`).
- Ship + thrust movement exist (`src/entities/Player.ts`, `src/utils/movement.ts`, `GymPlayer.ts`).
- GDD §4.4 defines P3/P4/P6/P7 semantics and icon suggestions; §4.4 notes Bomb does not damage 1-HP enemies; §2.3 lives model (out of scope here, replaced by flash/reset).
- Tests use Vitest + a gameHarness (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`) with happy-dom.

## Desired change

1. Extend the power-up catalogue from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT with **P3/P4/P6/P7** entries (id, name, icon, duration/stack semantics, threat-coupled effect hooks), following the same `src/powerups/` layout.
2. Add `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — ship (reused `Player` + movement), a Scout V-formation with a SHOOT toggle (bullets aimed at the ship), the shared round-robin spawner (P3 → P4 → P6 → P7), grow/hold/shrink lifecycle, 3% collection gate, threat-coupled effect application (shield absorb, bomb clear, phase shift pass-through, teleport safe-spot), flash/reset hit response, HUD attachment (reused), back button.
3. Ship-aimed fire: extend or parameterise the Scout's fire target so bullets aim at the ship's live position (implementation may pass the ship position into the scene's fire-collection path).
4. Add safe-spot resolution (enemy/bullet-aware) + teleport consumption to `src/powerups/effects.ts`; add hit-check suppression for shield/phase-shift in the scene collision pass.
5. Update the GDD §6.4 architecture briefly (list `GymPowerUpsCombat`; note threat-coupled effects as implemented).
6. Tests: unit tests for P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviours + scene tests via gameHarness.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — **new** combat gym scene (the deliverable).
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — extend the catalogue from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT with **P3/P4/P6/P7** entries.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — extend with shield-absorb state, bomb bullet-clear, phase-shift hit suppression, teleport safe-spot resolution + FIFO consumption.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — extend with P3/P4/P6/P7 code-drawn icons.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` — **reused** (depends on AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — **reused unchanged** (depends on AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` — possibly parameterised aim target (ship position) for `tryFireAimedBullet`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` (+ P3/P4/P6/P7 unit tests) — **new** tests.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — teleport safe radius + travelled distance, hit-reset values (extend the shared constants).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §6.4 architecture: add `GymPowerUpsCombat`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** — "Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD" (the non-combat gym): **prerequisite** — supplies the shared PowerUp lifecycle, catalogue, icons, HUD class, and spawn/lifecycle constants this item reuses/extends. Dependency edge: this item → AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT.
- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene" (in-progress): sibling — weapon power-ups excluded here, same round-robin/grow-shrink/3% mechanics.
- **"Create E1 Scout gym scene" / GymScout** — precedent for the Scout formation, EXPLODE/SHOOT buttons, and the `GymFormationScene` core-library pattern (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q completed; core-library refactor AH-0MT987VA3005YBNK / AH-0MTAN4IFR007U9B3 completed).
- **"Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement" (AH-0MT97OA3E001DOYW)** — precedent for `Player` reuse.
- GDD power-up catalog items (completed): "Redesign P7 Dash…" (AH-0MT7UY5UR002LD5U), "Add a Magnet power up" (AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V), "Add an extra life power up" (AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3) — semantics source for P7/P9/P8 (P3/P4/P6 remain as defined in GDD §4.4).
- GDD items (completed): "Game Design Document for AI_Hell" (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Dependency:** this item assumes the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) lands first (PowerUp lifecycle, catalogue, HUD, constants). If that item is delayed, the combat scene work is blocked — do not build parallel copies of the lifecycle/HUD.
- **Assumption — ship-aimed fire:** Scout's `tryFireAimedBullet` currently aims at a fixed demo target; the combat scene requires bullets aimed at the ship's live position. Implement by parameterising the aim target (small, contained change) rather than duplicating the Scout entity.
- **Assumption — teleport safe spot:** "nearest safe spot in the travel direction" = first empty position along the travel ray where no enemy body or bullet occupies a safety-radius disc (tunable, proposal 3× ship size), clamped to screen bounds; fallback = nearest on-screen safe position (GDD); P6 granted on arrival.
- **Assumption — hit response flash/reset:** a hit without shield/phase shift flashes the ship and repositions it (or grants brief invulnerability) — exact demo values tunable; no lives, no game over (operator Q8).
- **Assumption — scout formation counts as the "low-level threat":** default V-formation of ~6 scouts with drift (as GymScout), SHOOT toggle default OFF so the operator/player can turn fire on for the demo.
- **Scope-creep guard:** E2/E3/E4/E5/Boss threats, weapon autofire, lives/score, leaderboard, and the non-combat power-ups (P5/P8/P9) are out of scope; record any extras as linked work items.
- **Risk — sibling drift:** same constants/mechanics as the two sibling gyms; coordinate to keep the shared lifecycle consistent (extract a shared util if a third consumer appears).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (this round): "Which enemies constitute 'low level enemy threats' — reuse existing E1 Scout/E2 Diver/E3 Tank entities with bullet-firing, or generic placeholders?" — Answer (operator): **"1. Just use scout (with shooting)"** — the combat scene reuses the existing E1 Scout entity with its shooting enabled. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 (this round): "Ship hit response in the combat gym — (a) lives with respawn (3 lives), (b) simple flash/reset without a lives counter, (c) other?" — Answer (operator): **"2. b"** — simple flash/reset, no lives counter (pure demo). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3 (scope split, previous round): "Separate the combat-coupled power-ups (P3/P4/P6/P7) into their own work item and combat scene with low-level enemy threats?" — Answer (operator): **"Separate out the combat coupled items into a different work item and different combat scene. That scene should contain low level enemy threats."** — implemented as this item; the threat-free gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) keeps P5/P8/P9 and the shared lifecycle/HUD. Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q** – Create E1 Scout gym scene (completed)
- **AH-0MTAJO038004ILN8** – Gym index browser crash from bundled test files (completed)
- **AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5** – Game Design Document for AI_Hell (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mt7o8kcy0059ra5, 0mt7ve4sx0005a8v, absorb, absorbs, ac1 (+302 more)
- `README.md` — matched: ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance, active (+276 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: active, add, agents, aim, aimed (+178 more)

# Extend shared constants with combat-gym values

## Summary
Add combat-gym-specific tunable constants to `src/core/constants.ts` to complement the shared spawn/lifecycle constants from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 - Teleport safe radius constant:** A `teleportSafeRadius` constant is defined in `src/core/constants.ts` (proposal: ~3x ship size in pixels, tunable via named constant).
- [ ] **AC2 - Hit-reset values:** Constants for hit-response flash/reset behaviour are defined: `flashResetDuration` (invulnerability window, e.g. 0.5s), `flashResetRepositionX/Y` (or reposition offset), all in `src/core/constants.ts`.
- [ ] **AC3 - Constants are importable:** The constants are exported and can be imported by both the effects module and the combat scene without circular dependencies.

## Deliverables
- Extended `src/core/constants.ts` with combat-gym constants
- No other files modified

## Key Files:
- `src/core/constants.ts` - add teleport safe radius, hit-reset duration, reposition offset

# Remove the gap between Scout advance cue and shot (AH-0MTF1I1S8003P0GU)

**Headline:** The E1 Scout's firing audio feels disconnected — its ≥ 500 ms advance cue plays at tell start, then a dead gap, then the fire sound + shot at tell end. Restructure the Scout's tell audio so the fire sound is scheduled back-to-back at the cue's end (Tank-style no-gap treatment, per operator feedback from AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE), so cue flows directly into the shot with no gap while the shot still lands ≥ 500 ms after the cue starts (GDD §7.3).

## Problem statement

Scout (GDD §4.1 — E1) announces each aimed shot with a per-entity two-phase tell: `tryFireAimedBullet()` plays the ≥ 500 ms advance audio cue (`playScoutAdvanceCue()`) when the tell starts, then — after the 600 ms tell window elapses — fires the bullet and plays the fire sound (`playScoutFireSound()`) on a later tick. The operator hears this as cue → dead silence → disconnected shot blip. During intake for Tank audio (AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE) the operator directed the same no-gap treatment applied to Tank — cue must flow into the shot sound with **no gap** — and explicitly asked for a follow-up for Scout (created as this item, `discovered-from:AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE`). The disconnected feel was also noted in the Swarm playtest.

## Users

- **Players** — need audible feedback where the Scout's rising advance cue flows directly into a sharp shot blip (no dead air), so the firing event reads as one connected telegraph-and-shot gesture rather than two unrelated sounds.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need the Scout audio change to follow the established no-gap pattern (Tank precedent: fire sound scheduled at the cue's end, called back-to-back in the same tick) so headless tests stay green and the enemy core-library best practices apply.

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want the Scout's advance cue to flow straight into the shot sound with no dead gap so the aimed shot feels connected and readable.
- As a player, I still want ≥ 500 ms advance warning before each aimed Scout shot so I can react (GDD §7.3).
- As a developer, I want the no-gap change implemented via the existing `effects.ts` helpers so it degrades to a safe no-op in headless tests and never breaks the two-phase tell's shot timing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **No-gap audio flow** — The Scout's fire sound is scheduled to start exactly at the end of the advance cue (back-to-back, no dead gap between cue and shot sound, mirroring the Tank `TANK_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` pattern in `src/audio/effects.ts`), and the pair is invoked together at tell start.
- **Tell timing preserved** — The Scout's two-phase tell still gates the bullet: the aimed shot (bullet creation) still occurs ≥ 500 ms after the cue starts (`SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` unchanged at 600 ms, `SCOUT_FIRE_INTERVAL` unchanged), per GDD §7.3; no gameplay-timing regression.
- **Once-per-shot audio** — Exactly one advance-cue call and one fire-sound call per aimed shot (both at tell start); no per-frame repeats, no double-play, no fire-sound call at the shot itself.
- **Safe degradation** — All audio calls remain safe no-ops without a working `AudioContext` (headless tests); firing still produces bullets in headless runs.
- **Documentation** — `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§3.1 best practices item 6 and §3.2 `GymScout` row) and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 updated to record Scout's no-gap cue→shot treatment; `README.md` E1 Scout section updated if it describes the old gap behaviour; code comments updated. All related documentation (including code comments) updated to reflect the changes; CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship skill owns it).
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Procedural Web Audio only — no audio assets (existing `effects.ts` pattern).
- Follow enemy core-library best practices (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3.1/§7); the base `GymFormationScene` already owns spawn/destruction audio — do not add entity destruction sound calls.
- Audio functions must degrade to safe no-ops in headless environments.
- Keep the ≥ 500 ms advance-lead requirement (GDD §7.3) — the visual shot must land ≥ 500 ms after the cue starts.
- Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Scout.ts` — `tryFireAimedBullet(now)` two-phase tell: when the fire interval elapses and not telling → tell starts (`_isTelling=true`, `_tellStartTime=now`), plays `playScoutAdvanceCue()` and returns no bullet; a later call (next tick at/after `_tellStartTime + SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION`) ends the tell, creates the bullet and plays `playScoutFireSound()`. `SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION = 600` (Scout.ts:57), `SCOUT_FIRE_INTERVAL = 1200`.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playScoutAdvanceCue()` = `blip(880, 1320, 0.6, 'sine', 0.08)` starting at `currentTime`; `playScoutFireSound()` = `blip(1400, 700, 0.12, 'square', 0.12)` starting at `currentTime`. The `blip()` helper has no start-offset parameter. **No-gap precedent:** `TANK_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION = 0.6` and `playTankFireSound()` schedules its thump at `currentTime + TANK_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` so, called back-to-back with `playTankAdvanceCue()`, the pair flows with no gap (effects.ts:94–160).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts:95–103` — established no-gap orchestration precedent (scene-level new-bullet detection; plays cue then fire sound back-to-back).
- `src/entities/Scout.test.ts` — audio test "plays the advance cue once at tell start and the fire sound exactly once at the shot — cue precedes shot" (line ~228) asserts the CURRENT behaviour (fire sound only at the shot — must be updated); tell-timing tests (bullet at tell end) stay valid. Headless no-op test (line ~316) stays valid.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.test.ts` — AC6 real-timed test (line ~184) spies `playScoutFireSound` and asserts one fire-sound call per shot (`calls >= shots`, `calls <= scouts.length * 2`) — remains valid because the fire sound still plays exactly once per aimed shot (at tell start) under the new design.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3.1 item 6 — "Scout and Phaser use a per-entity two-phase tell — an advance cue (≥ 500 ms lead) at tell start, then the fire sound at the shot"; §3.2 `GymScout` row — "advance cue (≥ 500 ms) + fire sound (entity-level, per aimed shot)" (line ~168–190).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 — "Per-Enemy Audio Character" note records the Tank no-gap example and cross-references the enemy design doc; "Advance Telegraphing (≥ 500 ms Lead Time)" requires a short warning tone before Level 4–5 enemy fire.
- `README.md` E1 Scout Gym Scene section (line ~372) — describes "a per-entity advance cue ≥ 500 ms before the shot, then play the Scout fire sound at firing".

## Desired change

- **`src/audio/effects.ts`:** add `SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION = 0.6` (seconds, mirroring `TANK_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION`) and restructure `playScoutFireSound()` to schedule its blip at `ctx.currentTime + SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` (the cue's end time) so it lands exactly as the cue ends — called back-to-back with `playScoutAdvanceCue()` there is no dead gap (Tank-style). Keep the existing Scout sound characters (rising sine cue, sharp square shot) unless implementation determines otherwise; safe no-op guard preserved.
- **`src/entities/Scout.ts`:** at tell start invoke the pair back-to-back — `playScoutAdvanceCue()` then `playScoutFireSound()` (same tick; fire sound scheduled at cue end) — and remove the fire-sound call at the shot (the bullet still spawns at tell end, exactly when the scheduled fire sound lands). Tell state machine, `SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` (600 ms) and `SCOUT_FIRE_INTERVAL` (1200 ms) unchanged; update the class doc comment and `tryFireAimedBullet()` doc.
- **Tests:** update `Scout.test.ts` audio test to assert the fire sound is called once at tell start (back-to-back after the cue) and NOT at the shot; keep ordering assertion (cue call before fire-sound call) and per-cycle counts; add an assertion that the scheduled fire sound lands at the cue's end (e.g. spy on `playScoutAdvanceCue`/`playScoutFireSound` call pairing). Keep tell-timing + headless no-op tests green.
- **Docs:** enemy design doc §3.1 item 6 and §3.2 `GymScout` row updated from gap-based description to the no-gap pattern (fire sound scheduled at cue end, pair invoked at tell start); GDD §7.3 per-enemy note extended to include Scout as a no-gap example (optional, keep minimal); README §E1 Scout wording updated to the no-gap description.

**Key Files:**

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — add `SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` (0.6 s) and restructure `playScoutFireSound()` to schedule the blip at the cue's end time (Tank-style no-gap); headless no-op guard preserved.
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` — invoke cue + fire-sound back-to-back at tell start; remove the fire-sound call at the shot; update doc comments; tell constants/timing unchanged.
- `src/entities/Scout.test.ts` — update the audio test (fire sound at tell start, paired with cue; not at shot); keep tell-timing and headless no-op tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.test.ts` — verify AC6 real-timed audio assertions still hold (one fire-sound call per shot); likely no change needed.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts` + `src/entities/Tank.ts` — reference only (established no-gap precedent); no change expected.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 per-enemy note: add Scout no-gap example (minimal).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §3.1 item 6 and §3.2 `GymScout` row updated to the no-gap pattern.
- `README.md` — E1 Scout Gym Scene section (line ~372) updated if it describes the old gap behaviour.

## Related work

- **Tank has no audio (AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE)** — completed/in_review; source of the operator's no-gap directive ("cue → thump back-to-back (no gap)"; "also create a work item to remove the gap from Scout") and the Tank `TANK_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` / scheduled-at-cue-end fire-sound precedent this item mirrors. Parent relationship: this item was created `discovered-from:AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE`.
- **Scout has no audio (AH-0MTCO1LDA008RA19)** — completed; created Scout's two-phase tell with the gap this item removes.
- **Swarm has no audio (AH-0MTCO1L74003CAQJ)** — in-progress; the playtest where the disconnected audio feel was noted.
- **Test: Per-scene — player/combat assertions + regression (AH-0MTECNKPC00954HH)** — completed; documents the Scout two-phase tell timing the tests exercise ("`+= SCOUT_FIRE_INTERVAL` → tick (tell starts) → `+= SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION` → tick (fires aimed at the live player)").

## Risks & assumptions

- **Tell-timing vs Tank-style ambiguity (recorded decision):** the operator's no-gap directive could be read as (a) keep the two-phase tell for the visible shot and only restructure the audio (fire sound scheduled at the cue's end) — the scope line "keep the >=500 ms lead requirement" and GDD §7.3 ("short warning tone before bullets fire") only hold under this reading for aimed shots, since an aimed bullet may reach a near player in << 500 ms; or (b) fire the bullet immediately at interval elapse (Tank-literal). **Assumption: (a)** — two-phase tell and all its timing are preserved; only audio orchestration changes. If the producer intended (b), the tell state machine and tell-timing tests would also change — flagged in the appendix.
- **Sound character preserved:** the cue stays a rising sine and the shot a sharp blip; only the *timing relationship* changes. If implementation finds a character change improves the no-gap flow, record it in a comment; default is no character change.
- **Test drift:** `GymScout.test.ts` AC6 asserts one fire-sound call per shot (`calls >= shots`); under the new design the call happens at tell start (one per shot) so the assertion holds, but the implementer must verify after the change.
- **Scope creep:** no other enemy audio work is implied (Diver is a separate pre-existing item; Phaser keep its own two-phase tell — its fire sound is also played at the shot per its own pattern and is NOT in scope unless the operator asks). Record extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.
